vultrum.options.punchy_hand_cache.toolti:
Reduces CPU overhead from Punchy's first-person shader checks when Iris is absent. Requires Punchy 2.8f-hotfix or 2.8g and a supported Vitrail version.

Hand animations are preserved. Off by default.
vultrum.options.occlusion_cull.tooltip:
Skips terrain hidden behind other terrain, found on the GPU each frame. Needs a Vitrail shader pack enabled at launch.

Turns itself off in open scenes, where it would cost more than it saves.
vultrum.options.shadow_face_cull.tooltip:
Draws only the light-facing sides of solid blocks into the shadow map, where the terrain between them and the light is drawn too. Shadows look the same. About 5% more FPS at noon in tests. Needs a Vitrail shader pack.

Paused for packs that voxelise their shadow pass.
vultrum.options.sunless_shadow.tooltip:
Leaves terrain that sunlight can't reach, such as caves, out of the shadow map. About 1% more FPS in tests, and shadows looked the same. Needs a Vitrail shader pack.

Paused for packs that voxelise their shadow pass.
vultrum.options.packet_budget.tooltip:
Handles at most 1 ms of the server's packets a frame, so a burst of new chunks spreads over several frames. Flying into new terrain at 32 chunks stuttered 37-84% less in tests.

Packets held back for 50 ms are all handled at the next frame.
vultrum.options.arena_cap.tooltip:
Limits each new buffer Sodium creates for terrain to 96 MiB, unless its terrain needs more. Creating a larger one stalled the GPU for up to 5 ms, a stutter each time loading terrain filled the old buffers.

Uses more video memory: up to 0.6 GB more when flying fast at 32 chunks.
vultrum.options.unload_budget.tooltip:
Removes about 0.25 ms of chunks a frame from Sodium's terrain (more while thousands wait), so the chunks that leave the view aren't all removed in one frame. Flying at 32 chunks stuttered about a third less often in tests, and the longest frame after a long teleport was less than half as long.

Chunks waiting to be removed keep their video memory a little longer.
vultrum.options.reclaim_thread.tooltip:
Tidies up after Sodium's discarded terrain buffers on a thread of its own. Without it, the frame after a garbage collection tidies up tens of thousands of them at once: up to 33 ms in tests.

The work moves to another CPU core; it doesn't get smaller.
vultrum.options.reload_registration.tool:
Registers about 2 ms of already-loaded terrain columns a frame after F3+A or a render distance change. Terrain reappears over several frames while the reload completes.

New chunk arrivals are handled immediately as before.
